docs.title: Japanese Verbs — Formal and Plain Forms
docs.text:
This document contains the verbs from my vocabulary list, organized by Japanese verb group and original vocabulary level.

Each section contains:

  3. Present Negative

  5. Past Negative

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• The Dictionary Form is the basic form of the verb and is also the Plain Present Affirmative form.
  • The Formal Present Affirmative form uses ます.
  • The Formal Present Negative form uses ません.
  • The Formal Past Affirmative form uses ました.
  • The Formal Past Negative form uses ませんでした.
  • The Plain Present Negative form uses the appropriate ない conjugation.
  • The Plain Past Affirmative and Plain Past Negative forms follow the conjugation rules of each verb group.
  • 有る is the verb ある. Its negative is conventionally 無い rather than 有らない.

docs.title: い-Adjectives
docs.text:
The adjective itself changes:

Affirmative:
大きい

Negative:
大きくない

Past:
大きかった

Past Negative:
大きくなかった

docs.title: な-Adjectives
docs.text:
The adjective itself generally does not change. The copula changes instead:

Affirmative:
元気だ

Negative:
元気ではない

Past:
元気だった

Past Negative:
元気ではなかった

When an adjective directly modifies a noun:

大きい犬
元気な人

The な is used before a noun with な-adjectives.

docs.title: Japanese て-Form
docs.text: The て-form is one of the most important verb forms in Japanese. It is used to connect actions and to build several common grammar patterns.

docs.title: Group 1 — Godan Verbs
docs.text:
The ending of the verb changes according to its final kana.

Dictionary Ending て-Form Example う・つ・る って 会う → 会って む・ぶ・ぬ んで 休む → 休んで く いて 歩く → 歩いて ぐ いで — す して 写す → 写して

docs.title: Exception
docs.text:
行く → 行って

Although 行く ends in く, its て-form is 行って.

docs.title: Group 2 — Ichidan Verbs
docs.text:
Remove the final る and add て.

食べる → 食べて
見る → 見て

docs.title: Pattern
docs.text: る → て

docs.title: Group 3 — Irregular Verbs
docs.text:
These verbs must be memorized.

する → して
来る → 来て

docs.title: 1. て + ください — Polite Requests
docs.text:
Use:

て-Form + ください

This means:

Please do something.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
見てください。
Please look.

docs.title: 2. Connecting Activities or Events
docs.text:
The て-form can connect two actions or events.

Aて、B。

This can describe:

  • Two activities.
  • A sequence of events.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
朝ご飯を食べて、学校へ行きます。
I eat breakfast and go to school.

The actions happen in sequence:

食べる → 食べて → 行きます

docs.title: 3. てもいいです — Permission
docs.text:
Use:

て-Form + もいいです

This means:

It is okay to do something.

You may do something.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
ここで写真を撮ってもいいです。
You may take pictures here.

A shorter form is also commonly used:

ていいです

For example:

ここに座っていいです。
It is okay to sit here.

docs.title: 4. てはいけません — Prohibition
docs.text:
Use:

て-Form + はいけません

This means:

You must not do something.

You are not allowed to do something.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
ここで写真を撮ってはいけません。
You must not take pictures here.

This form is commonly used for rules and regulations.

docs.title: 5. から — Giving a Reason
docs.text:
The て-form can connect an action or situation to a reason.

Aて、B。

However, when giving a direct reason with から, the basic structure is:

Reason + から、Result.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
疲れましたから、休みます。
Because I am tired, I will rest.

A more natural everyday pattern is:

疲れたから、休みます。
Because I am tired, I will rest.

docs.title: 6. ましょうか — Offering Help
docs.text:
Use:

Verb stem + ましょうか

This means:

Shall I...?

Would you like me to...?

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
手伝いましょうか。
Shall I help?

Important:

ましょうか is not formed directly from the て-form.

手伝う
→ 手伝います
→ 手伝いましょうか

The て-form is commonly used in another related pattern:

Verb て + あげましょうか

For example:

手伝ってあげましょうか。
Shall I help you?

At the N5 level, the basic form 手伝いましょうか is sufficient for offering help.

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
ここに名前を書いてください。

Show translation Please write your name here.

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
ちょっと待ってください。

Show translation Please wait a moment.

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
この本を読んでください。

Show translation Please read this book.

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
窓を開けてください。

Show translation Please open the window.

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:

Show translation Please speak Japanese.

docs.title: 2. Connecting Activities or Events
docs.text: The て-form can connect two or more actions that happen in sequence.

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
朝ご飯を食べて、学校へ行きます。

Show translation I eat breakfast and go to school.

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
本を読んで、寝ます。

Show translation I read a book and go to sleep.

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
家に帰って、テレビを見ます。

Show translation I go home and watch TV.

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
起きて、顔を洗います。

Show translation I wake up and wash my face.

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:
コーヒーを飲んで、仕事をします。

Show translation I drink coffee and work.

docs.title: 3. てもいいです — Permission
docs.text:
Use:

て-Form + もいいです

This means:

It is okay to do something.

You may do something.

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
ここで写真を撮ってもいいです。

Show translation You may take pictures here.

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
このペンを使ってもいいです。

Show translation You may use this pen.

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
ここに座ってもいいです。

Show translation You may sit here.

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
この本を読んでもいいです。

Show translation You may read this book.

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:
今、帰ってもいいです。

Show translation You may go home now.

docs.title: 4. てはいけません — Prohibition
docs.text:
Use:

て-Form + はいけません

This means:

You must not do something.

You are not allowed to do something.

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
ここで食べてはいけません。

Show translation You must not eat here.

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
この部屋に入ってはいけません。

Show translation You must not enter this room.

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
ここで写真を撮ってはいけません。

Show translation You must not take pictures here.

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
このペンを使ってはいけません。

Show translation You must not use this pen.

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:
ここで話してはいけません。

Show translation You must not talk here.

docs.title: 5. から — Giving a Reason
docs.text:
Use:

Reason + から、Result.

This means:

Because [reason], [result].

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
疲れたから、休みます。

Show translation Because I am tired, I will rest.

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
お腹がすいたから、食べます。

Show translation Because I am hungry, I will eat.

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
雨だから、家にいます。

Show translation Because it is raining, I will stay home.

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
明日、仕事がありますから、寝ます。

Show translation Because I have work tomorrow, I will sleep.

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:
日本語を勉強したいから、本を読みます。

Show translation Because I want to study Japanese, I read a book.

から itself is not a て-form construction. It is included here because it is another basic N5 way to connect a reason with a result.

docs.title: 6. ましょうか — Offering Help
docs.text:
Use:

Verb stem + ましょうか

This means:

Shall I...?

Would you like me to...?

docs.title: Example 1
docs.text:
荷物を持ちましょうか。

Show translation Shall I carry your luggage?

docs.title: Example 2
docs.text:
手伝いましょうか。

Show translation Shall I help?

docs.title: Example 3
docs.text:
窓を開けましょうか。

Show translation Shall I open the window?

docs.title: Example 4
docs.text:
写真を撮りましょうか。

Show translation Shall I take a picture?

docs.title: Example 5
docs.text:
駅まで行きましょうか。

Show translation Shall I go with you to the station?
